title: St Patrick's Day argument: DARPA as Corso's conduit

plain: A DARPA scientist named John Blitch says that during a St Patrick's Day argument in a DARPA office, he built the case that DARPA, the Pentagon's agency for advanced research, grew out of the Army section where Philip J. Corso worked under a General Trudeau. Corso is the man behind the book The Day After Roswell, which Blitch draws on, and Roswell refers to the 1947 crash in New Mexico said by some to involve a craft not from Earth. In Blitch's argument, DARPA became "the conduit to break up all the component Technologies and distribute them", which would mean crash material was quietly fed into American research.
